'''Bernard Steele Meyerson''' (born June 2, 1954) is an American solid state physicist. 

==Biography==
Meyerson is a native of [[New York City]], born on June 2, 1954.<ref name="aipprofile"/> After graduating from the [[City College of New York]],<ref name="2011pake"/> he completed a master's degree and doctorate at the [[City University of New York]], and began working for [[IBM]].<ref name="aipprofile">{{cite news |title=B. Meyerson |url=https://history.aip.org/phn/11606040.html |access-date=22 February 2022 |publisher=American Institute of Physics}}</ref><ref name="2011pake">{{cite news |title=2011 George E. Pake Prize Recipient |url=https://www.aps.org/programs/honors/prizes/prizerecipient.cfm?last_nm=Meyerson&first_nm=Bernard&year=2011 |access-date=22 February 2022 |publisher=American Physical Society}}</ref> 

Meyerson was elected a fellow of the [[American Physical Society]] in 1998, "for the invention of ultra-high vacuum chemical vapor deposition and its application to low temperature silicon epitaxy, especially the fabrication of SiGe heterojunction bipolar integrated circuits for wireless telecommunications."<ref name="apsf">{{cite news |title=APS fellow archive |url=https://www.aps.org/programs/honors/fellowships/archive-all.cfm?initial=M&year=2021&unit_id=&institution= |access-date=22 February 2022 |publisher=American Physical Society}}</ref> The APS awarded him the [[George E. Pake Prize]] in 2011.<ref name="2011pake"/> Meyerson received the [[J. J. Ebers Award]] in 2000 from the [[IEEE Electron Devices Society]].<ref>{{cite news |title=Past J.J. Ebers Award Winners |url=https://eds.ieee.org/awards/j-j-ebers-award/past-j-j-ebers-award-winners |access-date=22 February 2022 |publisher=Electron Devices Society, IEEE}}</ref> In 2002, Meyerson became an elected member of the [[National Academy of Engineering]].<ref>{{cite news |title=Dr. Bernard S. Meyerson |url=https://www.nae.edu/30614/Dr-Bernard-S-Meyerson |access-date=22 February 2022 |publisher=United States National Academy of Engineering}}</ref>
